summary: North Dakota is permissive for the roof rat. Its Board of Animal Health rule (NDAC 48.1-09-02) explicitly names 'rats' — alongside gerbils, guinea pigs, hamsters, mice, and sugar gliders — as EXEMPT from both nontraditional-livestock licensing AND importation/CVI requirements (unless the State Veterinarian invokes a disease-based override). Game & Fish jurisdiction excludes animals held in private ownership, and no prohibited-species list names R. rattus. So keeping, breeding, selling/giving, and importing a captive-bred roof rat is effectively unregulated. The only loose end is that the exemption says 'rats' generically — a one-email confirmation to the State Vet would lock species coverage. Never release one.

keep.why: NDAC 48.1-09-02 names 'rats' as exempt from nontraditional-livestock requirements, and NDCC 20.1-01-02 excludes animals 'held in private ownership' from 'wildlife' (so Game & Fish jurisdiction doesn't apply to a captive pet). No North Dakota statute or rule lists R. rattus as prohibited/restricted. No permit to keep one. (Exemption text says 'rats' generically; State-Vet override exists but isn't invoked.)
keep.governing_law: NDAC 48.1-09-02 (rats exempt); NDCC 20.1-01-02 (wildlife excludes privately-owned); NDAC 48.1-09-01-01.

breed.why: Because rats are exempt from nontraditional-livestock licensing (NDAC 48.1-09-02), the Category 2/3 breeder-license requirements don't apply, and no separate ND breeder permit for exempt rodents exists. Hobby breeding is unregulated (federal USDA/AWA may apply at commercial volume).
breed.governing_law: NDAC 48.1-09-02; NDAC 48.1-09-01-03 (Cat 2/3 license — N/A to exempt species).

sell_give.why: No ND pet-dealer licensing regime for exempt rodents was found; conventional livestock-dealer licensing covers regulated livestock, not exempt pet rats. No rule prohibits transfer/sale of R. rattus. Free rehoming and sale are unregulated at the state level.
sell_give.governing_law: NDAC 48.1-09-02; NDDA Livestock Licensing (doesn't cover exempt rodents).

transport.why: NDAC 48.1-09-02's exemption explicitly covers IMPORTATION requirements for rats — so no CVI or import permit is required to bring a pet rat into North Dakota by default (the State Veterinarian can impose requirements only if disease conditions warrant). In-state transport is likewise unregulated. Never release a roof rat.
transport.governing_law: NDAC 48.1-09-02 (importation exemption for rats); NDCC Title 36 / NDAC 48.1-13 (general CVI — not triggered for exempt species).

restrictions.summary: Never release a roof rat — it's a non-native species. Local ordinances may add limits — check your city/county. (The State Vet retains discretion to add requirements if a disease concern arises.)

sources.title: NDAC 48.1-09-02 — Importation Requirements ('rats' exempt from NTL + import requirements)
sources.authority: North Dakota State Board of Animal Health
